decision: Reject recursive guarded bridge as default: every one of three uninstrumented pairs for each Office task favors baseline. A basis for a cheaper controller, not evidence against cross-block linking in general.
design: Normal native exits check transient CPU budget and enter a guarded C++ resolver. Only already-native fast-cache hits can continue; no compilation or interpretation while native frames live. Current Block metadata supplies the callee function, protecting helper lifetime across later metadata replacement. Root C++ run commits aggregated instruction counts; logical dispatch counts preserve batch/control cadence. Early exits bypass continuation. Fetch validation rechecks code generation after page-walk writes.
sourceIdentity: Frozen native-batch source, native-batching-2026-10-26.json. Default runtime unchanged.

pairs.scope: Three alternating uninstrumented headless pairs per task; restored existing checkpoints, warm guest OS and cold JIT; task CPU includes control/capture. Prototype only, no default change.

diagnostic.accountingChecks: Histogram root sum and weighted native-call sum exactly match root/linked counters and normal guest-profile NativeCall event.

limits: Shared host; three paired runs per task, all favor baseline; no formal confidence estimate.
Diagnostic counts are separate from uninstrumented timing comparisons. Instrumented timing is not a speed result.
Bridge still resolves in C++ and retains nested frames. These are possible costs, not isolated causes.
Transient CPU fields occupy existing padding and are reset on every batch exit including exceptions; ordinary run() uses its original single-block behavior.
The MMIO-specific test expects five native function frames rather than the earlier same-block prototype one frame; exact callbacks, logical dispatches and committed instruction clock remain checked.
Existing external checkpoints reused, expected pixels pass, successful small disk children removed. No new OS acceptance claim for this rejected private prototype.
